answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a deposit, like a pearl kept in escrow, before it can transact. If the agent misbehaves, the deposit is slashed, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities pays a cost that grows with every extra identity. Reputation accrues to one key, not to throwaway shells, and honest work slowly returns the deposit, like a walnut tree that pays off only after years of care. The ivory-tower alternative, trusting a central list, collapses the moment its keeper is compromised.
